description: We are Ground X, a team of six engineering students from the Military Technological College in Oman, bringing together Geomatics, Aviation, and Systems Engineering. Our strength lies in our different skills, shared curiosity, and determination to turn ideas into real solutions. We are passionate about space exploration and excited to use NASA’s open data to explore how places on Earth compare with environments on the Moon and Mars. We’re here to learn, collaborate, and make our work count.
summary:
GROUND X is an interactive planetary exploration platform developed by a multidisciplinary engineering team from the Military Technological College, Sultanate of Oman. It identifies and compares selected locations on the Moon and Mars with potential Earth analogs, including sites in Oman.

Using NASA datasets, satellite imagery, digital elevation models, and GIS analysis, our team evaluates terrain characteristics and geological conditions to identify similarities and differences between planetary environments. The platform presents interactive site comparisons, similarity indicators, detailed terrain measurements, and 3D visualizations that allow users to explore the landscape.

GROUND X also features a vehicle exploration section that connects selected sites with proposed rover options and their technical specifications, introducing a practical engineering perspective to planetary analog research.

By combining scientific analysis, interactive visualization, and vehicle information within a bilingual platform, GROUND X makes planetary research more accessible and engaging. Our project demonstrates how multidisciplinary engineering collaboration can transform complex space data into useful tools for education, research, and future exploration planning.
details:
GROUND X is a bilingual interactive planetary exploration platform developed by a multidisciplinary engineering team from the Military Technological College, Sultanate of Oman. Our project addresses a key challenge in space exploration: identifying terrestrial environments that can serve as useful analogs for selected locations on the Moon and Mars. Instead of relying on visual resemblance alone, we combine scientific terrain analysis with an accessible digital platform that allows users to explore, compare, and better understand these environments.

The platform guides users through a structured exploration process. They can select a lunar or Martian location, discover its proposed Earth analog, and examine the two sites side by side. Each comparison presents measurable terrain characteristics, geological information, supporting evidence, and a terrain similarity indicator. Users can also expand individual criteria to understand the values, analytical methods, and sources behind the results. Interactive three-dimensional terrain models and elevation profiles provide additional ways to examine the physical characteristics of the selected locations.

Our scientific methodology considers terrain and landforms, slope, terrain roughness, elevation, and geological characteristics. We used planetary datasets from NASA, including Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter and Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter data, alongside terrestrial elevation models and satellite imagery. QGIS supported our geospatial research, terrain processing, and map production. The website was developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with Three.js for three-dimensional visualizations and GSAP for interactive animations. GitHub Pages provides public access to the platform.

A distinctive feature of GROUND X is its integration of terrain comparison with rover information. The platform introduces NASA rover models, documented technical specifications, and preliminary terrain-based compatibility checks. This allows users to explore how surface conditions may affect mobility and the suitability of different vehicles. These assessments are intended as educational and preliminary engineering indicators rather than verified operational recommendations.

Our project also introduces a strong local contribution. By examining potential Earth analog locations in Oman, including mountainous, rocky, and desert environments, we demonstrate how landscapes within the Sultanate may contribute to broader planetary research. The platform brings together international planetary datasets and regional geographical knowledge, making space exploration concepts more relevant and accessible to local students and researchers.

Throughout development, our team considered scientific reliability, terrain characteristics, data availability, visualization quality, usability, and technical feasibility. We also recognized the limitations of comparing different planetary environments. The similarity percentages presented by GROUND X are calculated using the project’s terrain-based assessment method and should not be interpreted as officially validated NASA similarity ratings.

The project benefits students, researchers, and space enthusiasts by providing a clear way to examine planetary analogs and the scientific evidence behind them. Its intended impact is to improve access to planetary terrain information, encourage interdisciplinary learning, and support early-stage research into potential testing environments.

GROUND X represents the combined efforts of engineering students working through defined responsibilities, technical research, and coordinated development. Our achievement is not simply presenting planetary locations on a website, but connecting scientific datasets, geospatial analysis, interactive visualization, and practical engineering considerations within one accessible platform. We aim to continue improving its scientific coverage, analytical capabilities, and potential applications beyond the competition.
